industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the first European consumer readings in six weeks on its side and the tape's disagreement narrower. German consumer confidence (GfK) reads -30.8 for November from -30.6 and the euro area's flash reads -17.9 for October from -16.5 (Newsquawk, undated): low and edging lower, so the condition 'to D on a European consumer reading that is not falling' is tested and not met. The United States reading is disputed (University of Michigan 51.0, a three-month high, 6 November, against outlets describing it as falling). Relative strength, 2026-11-13 against 2026-09-11, not week on week: D now, D prior at the industry (C at last week's reading), with Online retail A, Hotels B (A last week), Apparel B and Physical retail B, so the second condition (the industry at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A) is not met either. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). Counter-case: the survey readings are undated headlines, four sectors still read A or B, 20 Pool stocks sit under this letter, and cyclicals led over the last week. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or the industry back at C with Online retail holding A.

sector.key: H.14. Automotive - retail, aftermarket, leasing and rental
sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral. The Neutral was an exception inside a Double Underweight industry, held because relative strength B offset the regime; the offset is gone (Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: D now, C prior) and the regime's consumer-and-financing read strengthened. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): big-ticket, financed consumer purchases under a record-low US current-conditions reading (University of Michigan 44.7), every house expecting consumer spending to slow into winter, and the hiking path pulled forward. One live holding, D'Ieteren (2.50%, Sell-side Momentum F), judged in component 4. Counter-case: no source spoke to autos or their retail this week, repair and aftermarket demand is less discretionary than new-car sales, and the European consumer itself was not read; back to C on a European consumer reading that is not falling.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Underweight named and judged thin. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) names 'worrying debt dynamics' in Belgium alongside France, Belgium, Austria and Finland; that is one clause in one note with no spread reading, the same footing on which Ireland was held Neutral last week for Overweight, so the row does not move on it. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to D if a second source names Belgium or a spread reading is read widening.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
